questions.question: For a square linear transform of size d-by-d applied to vectors of length d, which parameter count is correct for a low-rank factorization with rank r (assuming r << d) and why is it attractive compared to a dense matrix?
questions.choice_A: It uses 2dr parameters (U in R^{d x r} and V in R^{r x d}), which can be much smaller than d^2 when r << d
questions.choice_B: It uses r^2 parameters, which scales sublinearly in d
questions.choice_C: It uses d log d parameters, matching butterfly-like structures
questions.choice_D: It uses d + r parameters, dominated by biases

questions.question: Consider applying a product of k dense d-by-d matrices to a single d-dimensional vector during inference (no batching). What is the time complexity of the forward pass under a naive implementation?
questions.choice_B: O(k d^2)
questions.choice_C: O(k d log d)
questions.choice_D: O(k d)

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the computational cost of the backward pass for linear layers relative to the forward pass?
questions.choice_A: Backward is always cheaper than forward by a factor of 1/2
questions.choice_B: Backward is exponentially more expensive in the number of factors
questions.choice_C: Backward typically costs a constant-factor more than forward (often about 2–3x) with the same big-O scaling
questions.choice_D: Backward has the same FLOPs as forward but much larger asymptotic complexity

questions.question: You factorize a dense layer into a product of k structured layers (staged multiplications) and train end-to-end. What happens to the space complexity for activations during training if you store all intermediates for backprop?
questions.choice_A: It stays the same as the unfactorized layer
questions.choice_B: It decreases because each stage is smaller
questions.choice_C: It becomes O(d^2) due to Jacobian storage
questions.choice_D: It increases to O(k d) for vector inputs (or O(k n d) for batch size n), since you must keep k intermediate activations

questions.question: For small batch sizes at inference time, which factor most often dominates latency for large d transformations on modern accelerators?
questions.choice_A: Memory bandwidth and kernel launch overhead rather than raw FLOPs
questions.choice_B: Arithmetic throughput, since compute always dominates
questions.choice_C: Disk I/O for model weights on every call
questions.choice_D: PCIe transfer to host memory for every intermediate tensor

questions.question: Two algorithms have the same asymptotic complexity O(d log d). Why might one still be slower than an O(d^2) method for practical d?
questions.choice_A: Because O(d log d) always has higher memory complexity
questions.choice_B: Because constant factors, data layout, and bandwidth limits can make the lower-asymptotic method slower until a crossover point
questions.choice_C: Because O(d log d) implies more parameters than O(d^2)
questions.choice_D: Because O(d^2) methods parallelize worse on GPUs

questions.question: Which statement about butterfly-like parameterizations for d-by-d transforms is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: They use exactly d parameters
questions.choice_B: They use O(d log d) parameters by composing sparse, structured stages
questions.choice_C: They use O(d^2) parameters but fewer FLOPs
questions.choice_D: They use O(log d) parameters if implemented recursively

questions.question: What practical profiling approach helps determine whether a given layer is memory-bound or compute-bound?
questions.choice_A: Counting parameters and comparing to latency directly
questions.choice_B: Roofline analysis, relating operational intensity (FLOPs/byte) to hardware peak FLOPs and bandwidth
questions.choice_C: Only measuring GPU temperature
questions.choice_D: Using asymptotic notation and ignoring constants

questions.question: You have a strict parameter budget for a deep network. What is a principled way to allocate parameters across layers?
questions.choice_A: Distribute parameters uniformly across all layers
questions.choice_B: Use layer-wise sensitivity analysis or ablations to concentrate parameters where loss is most sensitive to capacity
questions.choice_C: Allocate all parameters to the first layer
questions.choice_D: Allocate parameters inversely proportional to layer index

questions.question: Replacing a dense layer with a staged product of k low-rank factors reduces parameter memory. What is a likely impact on activation memory and latency?
questions.choice_A: Activation memory decreases and latency decreases
questions.choice_B: Activation memory can increase (more intermediates), and latency may increase due to extra stages
questions.choice_C: Activation memory is unchanged and latency is unchanged
questions.choice_D: Activation memory increases but latency always decreases

questions.question: A block-diagonal d-by-d matrix with b equal-sized blocks (and zeros elsewhere) has how many trainable parameters (ignoring biases)?
questions.choice_B: 2 d b
questions.choice_C: d^2 / b, since each block is (d/b)-by-(d/b)
questions.choice_D: d log b

questions.question: What is the forward-pass time complexity of applying a low-rank factorization W = U V (with U in R^{d x r}, V in R^{r x d}) to a single vector x in R^d?
questions.choice_A: O(d^2), because U dominates
questions.choice_B: O(r^2), from the rank bottleneck
questions.choice_C: O(dr), by computing y = U (V x) with V x in O(dr) and then U times a length-r vector
questions.choice_D: O(d), because rank reduces dimension

questions.question: For a product W = W_k ... W_2 W_1 of k factors, how does the cost of computing gradients with respect to each W_i compare to the forward pass cost?
questions.choice_A: It is sublinear in k due to shared intermediates
questions.choice_B: It is exponential in k due to chain rule expansion
questions.choice_C: It scales on the same order as k times the per-factor forward cost, up to a small constant factor
questions.choice_D: It is zero for orthogonal factors

questions.question: Which structure most directly improves cache locality (and thus can reduce memory stalls) when multiplying by a large matrix?
questions.choice_A: A fully dense matrix with random sparsity
questions.choice_B: A single low-rank factorization with large r
questions.choice_C: A block-diagonal matrix with contiguous blocks that fit in cache
questions.choice_D: A permutation matrix with random stride access

questions.question: Which statement best describes the impact of batching on latency and throughput during inference?
questions.choice_A: Batching always decreases both latency and throughput
questions.choice_B: Batching increases latency per example and decreases throughput
questions.choice_C: Batching tends to increase throughput by amortizing overheads but can increase per-example latency
questions.choice_D: Batching has no effect on either latency or throughput

questions.question: Suppose algorithm A costs 50 d log_2 d operations, and algorithm B costs 0.5 d^2 operations. At d = 1024, which is faster based on this simple cost model?
questions.choice_A: Algorithm B is faster because 0.5 d^2 < 50 d log_2 d
questions.choice_B: They are equal in cost at this d
questions.choice_C: Insufficient information; asymptotics are needed
questions.choice_D: Algorithm A is slightly faster: 50 * 1024 * 10 = 512,000 vs 0.5 * 1024^2 = 524,288

questions.question: Two models have nearly identical FLOP counts for a given input but show very different wall-clock latencies. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.choice_A: FLOPs exactly predict latency on all hardware
questions.choice_B: The model with higher latency must be compute-bound
questions.choice_C: They use different random seeds
questions.choice_D: Differences in memory bandwidth use, kernel fusion, and data layout cause different operational intensities and overheads

questions.question: How do optimizer states affect training-time memory footprint, and how does this interact with parameter-reduction strategies?
questions.choice_A: Optimizers do not store extra state beyond parameters
questions.choice_B: SGD with momentum doubles the activation memory only
questions.choice_C: Adam reduces memory because it compresses gradients
questions.choice_D: Optimizers like Adam store extra tensors (e.g., m and v), making memory roughly 2–3x parameters; reducing parameters via structure reduces this overhead too

questions.question: What is the effect of gradient checkpointing when training deep or staged linear transformations?
questions.choice_A: It reduces compute and memory simultaneously
questions.choice_B: It increases memory usage by storing more intermediates
questions.choice_C: It has no effect on training dynamics
questions.choice_D: It reduces activation memory by discarding intermediates and recomputing them during backward at extra compute cost

questions.question: You must meet a strict parameter budget and a latency target when replacing dense layers with butterfly-like or low-rank factorizations. Which design choice is most relevant to balance these constraints?
questions.choice_A: Only the learning rate schedule
questions.choice_B: Adding biases to every stage
questions.choice_C: Randomly permuting inputs between stages
questions.choice_D: Choosing the number of stages and per-stage sizes/ranks to trade parameters against the number of sequential multiplications (which affect latency)
